key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling fruit juice on credit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) discouraged selling fresh fruit juice (asir) on credit due to the risk of fermentation turning it into wine during the delay period, thereby altering its legal status from permissible to impure or prohibited. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of preventing uncertainty (gharar) and preserving the purity (taharah) of consumables by linking the commodity's state to the duration of the credit term.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazeed Bin Khaleefa who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> disliked selling the juice with a delay (on credit, lest it turns into wine)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ibn Muskan from Yazid ibn Khalifah who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, disliked selling juice for deferred payment.”
